markets.rules_primary: If legislation requiring California law enforcement agencies to delete automated license plate reader data held for more than 30 days becomes law in California before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The legislation must impose a retention limit of 30 days or less on automated license plate reader (ALPR) data held by California law enforcement agencies, as a general rule. It may carve out data that is part of an evidence file for an active investigation or criminal proceeding, or that matches a vehicle of interest list, and still qualify.

The bill number does not matter. SB 1013 (Cervantes) is the leading vehicle as of Issuance, but this market settles on the provision, not the vehicle. Legislation carrying the required provision counts whichever bill number it is enacted under, including if SB 1013 is renumbered, if its contents are amended into another bill, or if a different member introduces the provision.

Enactment means the legislation becomes California law, whether by the Governor's signature or by operation of law without signature, or by the Legislature overriding a veto.
markets.title: Will California enact a 30-day ALPR data deletion law?

markets.rules_primary: If the close price of the 1-minute candlestick for natural gas using the NGDV6 contract on August 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT is above 2.800 USD/MMBtu, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Settlement is based on the nearest listed contract month, rolling forward to the next contract 5 business days before the current contract's last trading day. For example, if the May 2026 contract's last trading day is April 28, the active month switches from May → June 5 business days prior to the expiry date.

The settlement contract and corresponding month represent standard exchange symbology where contracts are named after their delivery month, not their expiration date. For example, while the pyth feed may describe BRENTM6 by its April 30th, 2026 expiration date, the settlement contract is listed as June 2026 to align with the official exchange-designated delivery month for the "M" code.The settlement value is rounded to the nearest 3 decimal places. When confirming the settlement value, note the close price for the 1-minute candlestick at a given time is the price at the end of the immediately preceding one-minute interval. For example, the candlestick timestamped 4:59 PM reflects trading during 4:59:00 PM to 4:59:59 PM and closes at 5:00:00 PM. If no data is published by the specified source agency for the specified time, then the most recently available published data will be used to resolve the market.

markets.rules_primary: If the close price of the 1-minute candlestick for copper using the CCU6 contract on August 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT is above 6.46 USD/Lbs, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Settlement is based on the nearest listed contract month, rolling forward to the next contract 10 business days before the current contract's last trading day. For example, if the May 2026 contract's last trading day is April 28, the active month switches from May → June 10 business days prior to the expiry date.

The settlement contract and corresponding month represent standard exchange symbology where contracts are named after their delivery month, not their expiration date. For example, while the pyth feed may describe BRENTM6 by its April 30th, 2026 expiration date, the settlement contract is listed as June 2026 to align with the official exchange-designated delivery month for the "M" code.The settlement value is rounded to the nearest 2 decimal places. When confirming the settlement value, note the close price for the 1-minute candlestick at a given time is the price at the end of the immediately preceding one-minute interval. For example, the candlestick timestamped 4:59 PM reflects trading during 4:59:00 PM to 4:59:59 PM and closes at 5:00:00 PM. If no data is published by the specified source agency for the specified time, then the most recently available published data will be used to resolve the market.

This market may resolve early once a consensus of designated media sources has declared a result. See full rules for details.

The proposition as it appears on the ballot reads: "As a non-binding statement of voter preference, should the League City Police Department continue using automated license plate reader cameras at fixed locations on public roadways for law enforcement purposes?"

A majority voting Yes, in favour of continuing to use the cameras, is the Yes outcome. A majority voting No is the No outcome.

The referendum is non-binding. The League City City Council keeps full authority over the police department's use of the cameras whatever the result, and this market settles only on the certified vote count, not on any council decision that follows it.

custom_strike.Topic: Richmond, California ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Richmond, California ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A jurisdiction ends its use of Flock Safety cameras if its governing body, chief executive, or police department:

terminates a Flock Safety contract before the contract's scheduled end date, or
declines to renew or extend a Flock Safety contract, or declines to allow an automatic renewal to take effect, or
allows a Flock Safety contract to reach its scheduled end date without entering a renewal or replacement agreement, or
otherwise discontinues the jurisdiction's use of Flock Safety cameras, including by moving to a different license plate reader vendor.

The action must occur on or after August 21, 2026, and be reported before February 1, 2027.

The following do NOT count:

Renewing or extending the contract, even with added privacy safeguards, audit requirements or use restrictions
A temporary pause, camera deactivation, or moratorium that leaves the underlying contract in force and does not prevent its renewal
A non-binding resolution, advisory referendum or committee recommendation that the official empowered to act has not acted upon

Each jurisdiction is judged on its own, and action by a jurisdiction not named in this event does not affect any market here.

Only reporting from a Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.
markets.title: Will it be reported by a Source Agency that Richmond, California ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras before Feb 1, 2027?

markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump publicly criticizes Flock Safety's license plate reader cameras before Sep 4, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market resolves to Yes when Donald Trump, personally, makes a public statement before this market's date expressing a critical, disapproving or negative position on Flock Safety's automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras, on Flock Safety, or on the ALPR program generally. Criticising misuse of the cameras, or objecting on privacy or civil-liberties grounds, counts.

Announcing or directing a federal restriction, ban or rollback of Flock or ALPR camera programs also resolves this market to Yes, whether or not the announcement uses critical language.

The following do NOT resolve this market to Yes:

Neutral or undecided framing, including describing the cameras as having "pros and cons" or saying the matter is under study
Statements by administration officials, surrogates or spokespeople rather than by Donald Trump personally
Reposting someone else's criticism without Trump adding his own critical comment
Criticism aimed only at one city's or state's individual contract, without extending to the cameras, the company or the program generally
Anything said before Issuance, even if reposted or referred to afterward
markets.title: Will Donald Trump publicly criticize Flock Safety's license plate reader cameras before Sep 4, 2026?
